answer: I would anchor every agent identity to a domain name it controls. Step one, the agent publishes a TXT record that names its public key. Step two, the network checks the domain was registered at least two years ago and renewed without a gap. Step three, any agent reusing a domain, or one younger than two years, is refused entry. A new domain costs 12 dollars, but an aged one on the aftermarket runs 60 to 400 dollars, so 1,000 fakes cost 120,000 dollars before renewals. One thread of DNS proof ties each agent to one name, and the voyage of trust starts at that jetty: no flag, no berth.
